reasons: The cited Section 14.3 is the operative governing-law/venue provision and the finding quotes it accurately; California law is expressly within the playbook's fallback set (Delaware or California law and courts).

The walk-away trigger is not engaged: there is no vendor home-jurisdiction law outside the accepted list and no arbitration seated abroad — the AAA seat is San Francisco County, California, with enforcement in the San Francisco courts, i.e. a domestic forum, consistent with the rule summary's concern about 'foreign arbitration'.

The shortfalls against the preferred position (California rather than New York law; arbitration rather than direct recourse to courts) are correctly treated as sub-elements noted in the rationale rather than material fallback failures, and the fee-allocation mechanic is symmetric, so it does not disadvantage us.

Consistent with a compliant claim, no redline or counterparty comment was produced — the rendered text is identical to the original and the deterministic jurisdiction check passes, so the finding is properly retained as internal evidence rather than raised as a negotiation issue.
